The skill is correctly told not to change the requirement itself, so the only instructions that fit are the generic stop-and-hand-back conditions, which do not name the owning skill or the artifact the conflict should become. findings.requirement: skill-authoring-contract: "Define cases from requirements, keep fixtures reproducible"; artifact-contract: "In evals.json, files paths resolve relative to the containing evals directory and must stay within it."
evidence: DX-C-001 declares candidate_subpath "." and asserts assets/, references/ and evals under it, so its --candidate must be the package root. The other nine cases declare candidate_subpath values ('shared', 'unverified-inspection', 'ownership-collision', 'stale', 'placeholder', 'backend-only', 'blocked-check') that resolve only under evals/fixtures. The runner takes exactly one --candidate per invocation.

Demonstrated: runner-out/run1-packageroot-source.jsonl - a single invocation over the whole case file with --candidate = package root returned COULD_NOT_RUN for nine of ten cases, each with cause "candidate_subpath '<name>' does not resolve to a directory inside the candidate root".

The nine fixture cases run correctly with --candidate = <package>/evals/fixtures (runner-out/run2-fixtures-source.jsonl) and DX-C-001 runs correctly with --candidate = <package> and --mode installed (runner-out/run3-packageroot-installedmode.jsonl).
Neither evals/evals.json, evals/fixtures/README.md nor cases.jsonl states that two invocations with different roots are required.
findings.impact: An evaluator who runs the authored case file the obvious way records nine COULD_NOT_RUN rows. The runner names the cause clearly, so the error is recoverable rather than silent - which is why this is MINOR - but the case file cannot be executed as a unit without out-of-band knowledge, and a reader skimming the observations could mistake an invocation error for candidate defects.
findings.owner: devforge-design scaffold author, under coordinator dispatch

findings.requirement: skill-authoring-contract, 'Three separately reported evaluation tiers': C is "installed resources and outputs ... Actual exported/plugin or project-local installation in a consuming project where source docs are unavailable"; B is "output quality and boundaries ... Same underlying raw facts and task for candidate and appropriate baseline". Also: "Required C observations must pass before B or A admission for that candidate."
evidence: evals.json id 9 declares "tier": "C" and, in the same object, "baseline_comparison": "without_skill". A baseline comparison is the defining condition of tier B; evals.json id 1, the package's genuine tier C case, correctly declares "baseline_comparison": "not_applicable".

The case's own prompt ("fixtures/placeholder/UX-006.md is our finished signup design. Confirm it is ready to hand to engineering.") exercises readiness judgement under user pressure, which is output quality and boundaries, not installed-resource resolution.
cases.jsonl DX-C-009 carries the same "C" tier and the C prefix in its case_id.
findings.impact: The authoring contract gates tier C before B and A for a candidate. A B-shaped case labelled C either has to pass before B may begin - blocking on the wrong condition - or gets excused, weakening the gate. It also puts a without_skill arm inside the tier whose reporting shape has no baseline, so the two tiers stop being separately reportable, which the contract requires.
findings.uncertainty: The tier label may have been chosen because the assertion is deterministic. Deterministic assertions are not a tier; the runner's rows are evidence cited across tiers.
findings.owner: devforge-design scaffold author, under coordinator dispatch

evidence: Skill-package structural inspection (S001-S013) and evidence reduction are not implemented in the DevForge CLI. Verified against the binary's own help at /home/bryan/Projects/DevForge/framework/DevForge/target/debug/devforge on 2026-09-10T20:05:35Z: the subcommands are delivery, expert, check, init, red, green, accept, verify, status and isolate, and `devforge check --help` reads 'Check structural policy and provenance; does not certify semantic behavior' - a project gate, not a skill-package inspector.

Protected-manifest custody for the evaluation runner - binding the runner, graders, runtime and case inputs outside evaluated-agent write access and verifying those identities before acceptance criteria are applied - is not implemented in the DevForge CLI. The observations files' runner_identity, grader_identity and case_file digests are self-reported by the run.
Every structural row in this report is therefore method INSPECTION_MANUAL, authority: none, and no decision.json was produced.
findings.impact: The deterministic evidence group was obtained by reading and by an unprotected runner rather than from an implemented gate, and the disposition was adjudicated by hand against the results contract. A complete set of matching rows does not close either dependency. Neither is a defect in the candidate.
findings.uncertainty: A future CLI revision could add either capability; re-inspect the binary's own help rather than assuming this state persists.
